generations.name: Original 911 / F-Body
generations.tagline: From 901 to Carrera RS: the legend begins
generations.description: On 12 September 1963, at the Frankfurt IAA, a two-seat-plus-two coupé with a flat-six behind the rear axle was presented as the successor to the 356 — but under the name 901. At the Paris Salon that October, Peugeot objected: it held the French trademark on three-digit model numbers with a zero in the middle. Porsche renamed the car 911 for all markets rather than sell a different name in France alone, keeping the 901 prefix on engine and parts numbers for years. Series production began in September 1964. Porsche's own model history states that 82 units were built as 901 before the switch, though Porsche Museum collection manager Alexander Klein has argued that number is a long-repeated error inherited from a misread record.

generations.name: G-Model & 930 Turbo
generations.tagline: Impact bumpers, turbochargers and sixteen years
generations.description: Porsche began series production of the second-generation 911 in August 1973 for the 1974 model year. The rework added telescopic impact bumpers that met the US 5-mph crash rule, a full-width rear light band, a longer and more comfortable body (4,291 mm) and — for the first time across the range — the 2.7-litre flat-six that had previously been reserved for the Carrera RS 2.7. The launch landed in the middle of the 1973 oil crisis, yet the car became the best-selling 911 to that point.

generations.name: Third Generation 911
generations.tagline: Modernity, all-wheel drive, and the last 911 turbos
generations.description: When the 964 arrived in late 1988 it looked like a mildly facelifted 911 but was in fact about 85 per cent new, and it quietly introduced features the model line had never had: all-wheel drive, power steering, ABS, an automatically extending rear spoiler, dual ignition with knock control, a three-way catalytic converter and — from 1990 — the Tiptronic automatic gearbox. The drag coefficient fell to 0.32, at the time the most aerodynamic 911 ever built, and coil springs on MacPherson struts front and semi-trailing arms rear replaced the old torsion-bar suspension for the first time in the 911's history.

generations.name: Last Air-Cooled
generations.tagline: The last air-cooled 911, and a modern classic
generations.description: The 993 was built from January 1994 to March 1998 as the fourth 911 and the last air-cooled Porsche. Tony Hatter’s redesign kept the silhouette but added flatter polyellipsoid headlights, integrated bumpers and a new LSA (Light, Stable, Agile) aluminium chassis with a multi-link rear axle that cured lift-off oversteer; only about a fifth of the parts carried over from the 964. The engine line ran from a 272 PS 3.6-litre flat-six to the 285 PS VarioRam car and the first biturbo 911, a 408 PS twin-turbo. The range widened into Carrera 4S and Carrera S, the 300 PS Carrera RS, the rear-drive GT2, the 450 PS Turbo S, plus rare Speedster and Turbo Cabriolet specials. Road production ended on 31 March 1998, and today the 993 is widely treated as the most desirable post-classic 911.

generations.name: Water-Cooled Turn
generations.description: Unveiled in 1997 and built from 1998, the 996 was the first series 911 with water cooling: tightening emissions rules demanded a four-valve cylinder head that only liquid cooling could keep reliable, and in doing so Porsche extracted 300 PS from the basic 3.4-litre flat-six. Designed by Pinky Lai under chief designer Harm Lagaay, the body was 18.5 cm longer and 3 cm wider than the 993 yet around 50 kg lighter, and it shared its front end and much of its structure with the 986 Boxster — a parts-sharing strategy that critics seized on when they mocked the shared headlight shape. A 2002 facelift brought 3.6-litre power, Turbo-derived styling and the Targa's powered glass roof, while the range ran from the Carrera all the way to the 483 PS GT2. Porsche built 175,262 examples between 1998 and 2005.

generations.name: Return of Round Lights
generations.description: In July 2004 Porsche put the sixth-generation 911 on sale with its most consequential styling correction since 1973: the "fried egg" headlamps of the 996 gave way to steeper, round clear-glass units with separate indicators, returning the car to the visual lineage of the air-cooled era. Designer Grant Larson's body was 88 mm (3.5 in) wider at the rear, with a drag coefficient of 0.28 for the Carrera and 0.29 for the Carrera S. Beneath the new skin the 3.6-litre flat-six made 325 PS (321 hp) and the newly developed 3.8-litre Carrera S 355 PS (350 hp) — the first 911 since 1977 offered with two naturally aspirated displacements and performance levels.

generations.name: Long-Wheelbase Era
generations.description: Unveiled at the Frankfurt Motor Show on 15 September 2011, the 991 was only the third all-new 911 platform since 1963 and, in Porsche's own words, the greatest engineering leap in the model's history: close to 90 per cent of its components were new or substantially redeveloped. The wheelbase grew by 100 mm (3.9 in) to 2,450 mm (96.5 in), the rear axle moved 76 mm (3.0 in) further back for better weight distribution, and an aluminium-steel body cut around 80 kg (176 lb) compared with the 997 despite extra equipment. It introduced the world's first seven-speed manual gearbox, and from the 2013 Turbo onwards offered active aerodynamics and rear-axle steering.

generations.description: Unveiled at the Los Angeles Auto Show on 28 November 2018, the 992 arrived as the eighth generation of the 911 and as the moment the wide body stopped being a privilege of the Turbo models: for the first time every car in the range — Carrera, Targa, GTS, GT3 — carries the flared rear arches and 20-inch front/21-inch rear wheels that had previously marked out only the top performers. Styled under Michael Mauer by Ben Baum, it grew 45 mm (1.8 in) wider than the 991 on an unchanged 2,450 mm (96.5 in) wheelbase, added aluminium body panels, pop-out door handles and a full-length rear light bar, and put the driver's instruments back into two screens either side of a central analogue rev counter.

generations.name: T-Hybrid Generation
generations.tagline: T-Hybrid: 541 PS, an eTurbo and 400 volts
generations.description: The 992.2 is the first 911 generation to carry a high-voltage electrical system, and Porsche's engineers arrived at the shortest possible route to it. Unveiled on 28 May 2024 alongside the revived Carrera, the debut model was the Carrera GTS with the T-Hybrid system: a 3.6-litre boxer with a single electrically assisted exhaust-gas turbocharger, a permanent-magnet synchronous motor buried inside the eight-speed PDK, and a 1.9 kWh, 400-volt battery no bigger than a conventional starter battery. The motor spins the turbo to speed before the exhaust gas arrives, so boost is instant — full system torque of 610 Nm is on tap below 2,000 rpm. Unlike a plug-in hybrid, the battery is never drained for propulsion; it is there to recover energy and to fill gaps. Porsche cites a weight penalty of just 50 kg over the outgoing GTS, against roughly eight times that for a typical PHEV.
